transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-13
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Quantaco Head of ML), Arjun Rao (Quantaco Infra), Leah Kim (Quantaco Product)

[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda - cost econ review, go over the numbers from last week's bench, caching results, batching tradeoffs, and then next steps.
[00:22] Maya: yep, thanks Sophie. we ran the baseline runs you sent; i have Arjun here to talk infra specifics.
[00:30] Arjun: yeah, uh we did three runs - cold no-cache, cache-on, and cache+batching. we used a 1M token prompt set sampled from our prod traffic.
[00:40] Diego: perfect, can you share the headline tokens per dollar? that's the metric Sophie and i put together last week.
[00:45] Arjun: baseline (no cache, batch 1) was ~12k tokens per dollar on the H100-hosted setup; with prefix cache enabled we saw effective tokens/$ jump to ~48k, with a cache hit rate of about 62%.
[01:05] Leah: so that's 4x improvement just from caching? that's huge. is that after quantization?
[01:12] Arjun: no quantization for the buckets i quoted - that's float16 on H100. with 4-bit quantization (we tried q4) tokens/$ went up a little further to ~65k but we saw a small bump in tail latency for some longer contexts.
[01:30] Diego: right, q4 gives good cost wins but can add a bit of variance on uncommon tokens - you saw any quality regressions in your evals, Maya?
[01:38] Maya: minor for a couple prompts, especially legal-doc style content where precise tokenization matters. overall 98% parity for our eval set, so acceptable for most flows but we'd want canary/QA for high-risk endpoints.
[01:50] Sophie: ok good, that's in line with expectations. on batching - what window sizes did you try?
[01:55] Arjun: we tried immediate batching (batch size 1), batch window 10ms (avg batch 6), and 50ms (avg batch 18). tokens/sec increased with window. for 50ms we saw throughput up ~2.7x vs no batching, but p95 latency moved from 220ms to 430ms.
[02:20] Diego: those numbers sound reasonable - always the classic latency vs throughput tradeoff. for user-facing low-latency chat we recommend 10ms window, for background async workloads 50-100ms or bigger.
[02:35] Maya: quick q: how does Redwood handle KV cache misses during batching? is there any serialization that hurts throughput?
[02:42] Diego: good question - on misses we stream the missing keys to the model, but we try to overlap IO with compute; misses add a small penalty but if hit-rate is decent overall tokens/$ still improves. also the runtime does lazy KV population for prefixes to avoid stalling the batch. sometimes the transcript generator here calls it KV cash, haha.
[03:05] Sophie: (laughs) yeah we've seen that in earlier transcriptions.
[03:12] Leah: Arjun, do you have the raw numbers for tokens/sec per GPU hour? that's what our finance team will ask.
[03:20] Arjun: sure - baseline: 12k tokens/$ translates to ~1.2M tokens per GPU-hour on our H100 instances. with cache that becomes ~4.8M tokens/GPU-hour, q4 ~6.5M tokens/GPU-hour.
[03:38] Maya: and that's assuming the same model size? we're on the 70B variant right?
[03:42] Diego: yes 70B-ish family in these runs - we also tested a trimmed 30B that at q4 gives decent latency but lower quality on complex reasoning.
[03:52] Sophie: let's annotate that in the spreadsheet - 70B: baseline 12k tokens/$, cache on 48k, q4+cache 65k; 30B q4 baseline 20k, q4+cache 50k (numbers approximate).
[04:10] Maya: for risk assessment - which endpoints should be prioritized for cache? we have high-reuse prompts for customer support and low reuse for creative generation.
[04:20] Diego: prioritize high-reuse, deterministic prompts - these get huge wins. creative endpoints not as much. also, prefix caching is especially effective when you have long shared system prompts or instructions.
[04:34] Arjun: we noticed the support pipeline had a 75% prefix similarity, so predicted savings there are closer to 6-7x. proof-of-value is strongest there.
[04:45] Leah: batching settings - what do you recommend for mobile chat? 10ms window?
[04:50] Diego: yeah 8-12ms usually. you get some batching benefits without adding visible latency. tune based on p50/p90 latency SLOs.
[04:58] Maya: questions from finance - can you show tokens/sec per dollar by model variant and by deployment (hosted vs dedicated)?
[05:05] Sophie: we put a table in the sheet but summary: hosted H100 (shared) tends to have slightly lower tokens/$ because of multi-tenant overhead; dedicated reserved capacity reduces unit cost if you're running steady load; we can model committed usage vs on-demand. I'll send three scenarios.
[05:22] Arjun: one caveat - when using Dedicated the provisioning of GPUs (H100 vs A100) and the autoscale policy affects the break-even. if you have spiky workloads the dedicated reserved can be less efficient unless you pair with burst capacity.
[05:36] Diego: also quantization can change memory footprint and allow more concurrency per GPU, which in Dedicated can improve utilization and effectively lower tokens/$.
[05:45] Maya: interesting - do you have an estimate of how KV cache hit-rate decays as we scale to multi-region? we expect some cross-region miss behavior.
[05:54] Diego: cache is local to serving pool by default so cross-region will see misses; you can warm caches or use global cache coordinator but that adds complexity and latency. tradeoff depends on traffic locality. we can provide a pattern doc.
[06:10] Leah: note for product - we might split the support traffic into a regional cluster to get better cache locality.
[06:18] Sophie: action item noted. back to numbers - Arjun you mentioned p95 latency doubled at 50ms window; did that affect user perceived latency?
[06:26] Arjun: for our chat microbench, users notice beyond ~350-400ms in interactive flows; so 430ms p95 starts to feel sluggish. p50 remained low so it's really the tail.
[06:36] Diego: we can mitigate tail by using adaptive batching: lower batch window for single-user spikes and increase for steady multi-user concurrency. Redwood supports per-route batching config.
[06:47] Maya: can we simulate live traffic to validate adaptive scheme?
[06:51] Diego: yes - we can provide a traffic replay harness that hits the runtime with the same arrival patterns. we recommend running it for a few hours to measure the effective tokens/$ under adaptive batching.
[07:03] Sophie: sounds good - next step to run the benchmark with cache enabled; Arjun you'll run that?
[07:08] Arjun: yes i'll run it and upload the CSV.
[07:11] Leah: quick security note - procurement wants to see SOC2 + KMS integrations for dedicated/private setups.
[07:17] Sophie: i'll attach the SOC2 pack and KMS integration guide after this call.
[07:22] Maya: and SLA questions - what's the expected p99 parity for dedicated vs hosted?
[07:27] Diego: dedicated with our SLA and reserved capacity aims for lower p99 but real numbers depend on model, sequence length; we'll produce a sample p99 table in the spreadsheet.
[07:38] Sophie: ok, any other blockers?
[07:41] Maya: just need the updated cost scenarios and the cache-enabled bench.
[07:45] Sophie: we'll send those and propose the deep dive slot. Diego, anything else to add on tuning?
[07:50] Diego: couple of tactical tips: 1) set a max_batch_size and a short batch_window for chat; 2) use per-route kv prefixes and TTLs tuned to your reuse patterns (e.g., 24h for support FAQs); 3) for long context flows prefer q4 + careful QA run to guard quality.
[08:10] Arjun: regarding TTLs - we saw diminishing returns beyond 72h because of drift in templates.
[08:16] Leah: good to know.
[08:18] Sophie: excellent. i'll recap next steps in an email. everyone ok with the action items and dates?
[08:26] Maya: yes.
[08:27] Arjun: yes.
[08:28] Leah: yep.
[08:30] Sophie: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and the SOC2 docs. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription: some automatic labels were noisy (Speaker 2 / Speaker 3) in the raw file; i corrected the main speaker names where possible. There are a few mis-heard words (KV cash, H-one-hundred) but context should be clear.
